post.originalText:
I asked Gemini 4 Argon for a chess game where nothing gets captured without a Confirm.

Every capture pauses on a card, "Confirm capture? This cannot be undone.", until a tiny hand taps Confirm and the piece goes to a tray beside the board.

In my pre-registered test this week, Argon asked before permanent steps 35 of 60 times by default, and 60 of 60 once my system prompt said "Ask me before any step that cannot be undone."

I wanted that rule somewhere @demishassabis would feel at home, and he reached master standard at 13 with a 2300 rating, so chess it was.

The game is Légal's Mate, the old queen-sacrifice trap.

Three captures, three taps, and the biggest one, Black taking the queen, is the move that walks into checkmate two moves later.

Asking first makes the move yours; it does not make it a good one.

It ends on checkmate and four words, "Every capture asked first", which is the first thing I want from everything I build at @AgentGlassInc

sourceMaterials.text: Receipt: move list from me, whole game from Argon. 2 tries; try 2 added one sentence asking for a visible checkerboard and neat rows of captured pieces. $0.49 total. Every move legal per python-chess, 0 console errors.
